newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian to boost Canada-U.S. capacity.
newsitem.headline: Canadian to boost Canada-U.S. capacity.

text.p: Canadian Airlines Corp said on Friday it planned to boost service between major aviation hubs in Canada and the United States in the final stage of its North American route restructuring.
Canadian said the new flights to the U.S. starting in the spring were the last phase of its schedule adjustment that was part of a massive restructuring that began in November.
The four-year plan includes boosting transborder capacity by 141 percent and Asian capacity by 21 percent this year.

Canadian said the new transborder service, which would use Canadian-operated aircraft, would include two daily flights between Vancouver and Dallas-Fort Worth, one daily flight between Vancouver and Chicago and new non-stop flights between Calgary and Chicago as well as Toronto and Dallas-Fort Worth.
All the new flights would be code-shared with partner AMR Corp unit American Airlines, Canadian said.
The route restructuring is part of a C$800 million life-support plan for struggling Canadian, which also included controversial wage cuts and a massive overhaul of its debt repayment obligations.

"Canadian is moving quickly to take advantage of new opportunities open to us in Vancouver under the Open Skies aviation policy," Canadian chief executive Kevin Benson said in a statement. "And with these changes we're entering an expanded phase in our relationship with American Airlines."
The two airlines code share on more than 700 flights a day.

Under the Open Skies agreement between Canada and the United States, restrictions on cross-border flights by U.S. carriers into Vancouver are set to be loosened in February, allowing American to take advantage of Canadian's strong access to Asia.
